kv-network-scheduler.title: KV-cache-aware network scheduler
kv-network-scheduler.problem: Prefill transfer and latency-sensitive decode traffic compete for network service.
kv-network-scheduler.mechanism: The scheduler tracks KV-cache location and decode urgency, then allocates network bandwidth between prefill and decode traffic.

evidence.claim: P99 request latency is reduced under the evaluated load.

kv-network-scheduler.limitations: At low load where inference is compute-bound, the scheduler provides little benefit.
kv-network-scheduler.project_relevance: The result supports exposing KV location and decode urgency to network scheduling rather than treating transfers as opaque flows.

dpu-inline-compression.title: DPU in-path compression
dpu-inline-compression.problem: Cross-region links may carry compressible object streams whose wire bytes, rather than codec compute, limit useful throughput.
dpu-inline-compression.mechanism: A DPU applies LZ4 compression before transmission and decompression on receive, with bypass for unsuitable payloads.

evidence.claim: Application-visible goodput increases for the compressible stream.
evidence.condition: compressible 256 MB object stream over a 400 Gbps path

dpu-inline-compression.limitations: Incompressible payloads should use bypass because compression can add latency without reducing wire bytes.
dpu-inline-compression.project_relevance: DPU compression is attractive only when codec throughput stays above link demand and compression ratio repays processing overhead.

chip-memory-bottleneck.title: Memory-path co-design for AI inference
chip-memory-bottleneck.problem: Decoder inference can be constrained by memory movement even when peak compute is unchanged.
chip-memory-bottleneck.mechanism: The design increases effective HBM bandwidth through a revised data-movement pipeline without changing the compute array.

evidence.baseline: same compute array with the original memory path
evidence.condition: batch-1 decoder inference for a 70B model

chip-memory-bottleneck.limitations: The gain shrinks for compute-bound matrix kernels, so the result should not be generalized to all workloads.
chip-memory-bottleneck.project_relevance: Chip evaluation should distinguish memory/data-movement bottlenecks from peak arithmetic capability.

cross-region-ec-loss.title: 6+2 EC-assisted cross-region transport
cross-region-ec-loss.problem: WAN loss can turn isolated missing packets into an RTT-scale retransmission penalty.
cross-region-ec-loss.mechanism: The transport uses a 6+2 erasure code across transfer blocks so isolated loss can be recovered locally instead of waiting for a full retransmission round.

evidence.claim: P99 completion time falls under the evaluated WAN loss condition.
evidence.condition: 80 ms RTT, 0.1% random loss, 64 MB transfers

cross-region-ec-loss.limitations: The 6+2 code adds 33% parity overhead and is unattractive on lossless or severely bandwidth-constrained paths.
cross-region-ec-loss.project_relevance: EC should be justified by retransmission avoidance under concrete RTT/loss conditions rather than by redundancy alone.
